explanation: A prophet in the Old Testament who received visions and messages from God.
The beginning of a series of chapters in Ezekiel that describe a vision of a new temple and its surroundings.
A holy place where people worship and offer sacrifices to God, usually central to Jewish faith and practice.
Indications of length, width, and height, used in Ezekiel 40 to describe the temple structure and its rooms.
A spiritual experience in which God or angels give information, guidance, or warnings to a person.
The outermost boundary or barrier around the temple, separating the holy area from the secular world.
Entrance areas of the temple that lead into the inner parts of the building.
A structure where offerings and gifts are presented to God as part of worship.
The most sacred place in the temple, where God's presence is strongest and only the high priest may enter.
